Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 16 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Union Cabinet Approves Rs. 4,371.10 Crore VISTAR Scheme to Modernise India’s Statistical System In November 2026, the Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, approved the Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR) Scheme, a Central Sector Scheme (CSS) with an outlay of Rs. 4,371.10 crore for five years from Financial Year 2026 -2027 (FY27) to FY31, aligning with the 16th Finance Commission cycle. • The scheme aims to establish a dynamic, agile and future-ready official statistical system capable of meeting evolving policy requirements, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Approval of the VISTAR Scheme ✓ Approved By: Union Cabinet chaired by PM Narendra Modi. ✓ Approval Date: 4 November 2026 ✓ Outlay: Rs. 4,371.10 crore. ✓ Implementation Period: FY27 to FY31 ✓ Scheme Type: Central Sector Scheme. ✓ Nodal Ministry: MoSPI ✓ Key Components: Statistical Operations, SSS and Economic Census. ✓ Major Survey Initiative: 59 surveys during the 16th Finance Commission cycle. ✓ Economic Census: 8th Economic Census. ✓ New Statistical Indices: Headline Index of Services Production and Index of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises. About VISTAR Scheme: Overview: Announced on November 4, 2026, the scheme will be implemented by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) to modernise India’s official statistical system through digital transformation, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and improved data governance. Reforms: The VISTAR Scheme builds on MoSPI’s recent efforts to update key statistical indicators, including the revised Consumer Price Index (CPI) series (2024 base year, February 2026), Gross Domestic Product (GDP) series (2022–23 base year), Index of Industrial Production (IIP) series (2022–23 base year, June 2026) and trial Index of Services Production covering 19 sub- sectors (July 2026). New Statistical Indicators: MoSPI plans to introduce the Headline Index of Services Production to measure services-sector output and the Index of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises to track the performance of unincorporated enterprises. Data Harmonisation: The scheme will enable standardised, interoperable and privacy-focused data sharing through machine-readable datasets, reducing duplication and fragmentation while improving programme targeting and AI-driven decision-making. Alternative Data Sources: MoSPI will integrate mobile phone, scanner and e-commerce data with traditional surveys to reduce respondent burden, address data gaps and strengthen evidence-based policymaking.

# Page 17^page=17
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 17 Daily Content PDF Capacity Building: The scheme will support students and researchers through internships, research proposals from academic and research institutions, and capacity-building initiatives to strengthen statistical capabilities. VISTAR Scheme: Three Major Components Comprehensive Statistical Operations and Strengthening of Ecosystem: Survey Expansion: MoSPI plans to conduct 59 surveys during the 16th Finance Commission cycle, up from 43 previously, to address sectoral data gaps and support timely, targeted policy decisions. Digital Transformation: MoSPI will digitise statistical processes end-to-end and integrate AI and Machine Learning (ML) into regular workflows for data processing, validation, analysis, statistical research and dissemination. Support for Statistical Strengthening (SSS 2.0) Development: VISTAR aims to strengthen the statistical capabilities of States and Union Territories (UTs), generate high-quality, granular data, develop indigenous data- processing capabilities and improve regional economic estimates for informed local policymaking. Data Expansion: MoSPI will provide technical support to develop district-level and million-plus city-level estimates under major statistical indicators, including the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES), Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE), GDP and IIP, along with the compilation of State-level and district-level GDP estimates and State-level IIP data. Eighth Economic Census: Census: MoSPI will conduct the 8th Economic Census (EC) in collaboration with State and UT Governments, which will serve as the baseline for developing the National Statistical Business Register (SBR). Coverage: The census will collect data up to the Gram Panchayat (GP) and Ward levels, providing a detailed assessment of India’s unorganised economic sector. About Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI): Formation: Established on October 15, 1999, through the merger of the Department of Statistics and the Department of Programme Implementation. • The first Economic Census was conducted in 1977 by Central Statistics Organisation (CSO) to map non-agricultural enterprises across India. Minister of State (MoS) (Independent Charge, IC) – Rao Inderjit Singh (Constituency: Gurugram, Haryana) Secretary – Saurabh Garg Cabinet Approves Rs 14,500 crore VGF Scheme for development of 92 GWh Grid-Scale Energy Storage Systems In November 2026, the Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, approved Rs 14,500 crore Viability Gap Funding (VGF) Scheme for Development of Grid-Scale Energy Storage Systems (ESS) for a period of 5 years i.e. from Financial Year 2026-27(FY27) to FY31. • The newly approved scheme marks a major step towards bolstering India’s power sector infrastructure, facilitating large-scale integration of Renewable Energy (RE) and ensuring reliable, affordable and 24×7 power supply.

# Page 18^page=18
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 18 Daily Content PDF • The Union Cabinet also approved a Capital Expenditure (Capex) Support Scheme, designed to promote domestic processing of critical minerals (including Lithium (Li) and Nickel (Ni)) with financial outlay of Rs 2,814-crore for a period of 5 years (from FY27 to FY31). Exam Hints: ✓ What? Approval of Viability Gap Funding Scheme ✓ Approved by: Union Cabinet, chaired by PM Narendra Modi ✓ Purpose: To develop grid-scale energy storage systems ✓ Outlay: Rs 14,500 crore (from FY27 to FY31) ✓ Target Capacity: 92GWh of new energy capacity ✓ Estimated Investment: Rs 97,600 crore ✓ Other Key Approval: Capex Support Scheme o Total Budget: Rs 2,814-crore (from FY27 to FY31) o Purpose: To promote critical mineral processing o Target Minerals: Li and Ni o Proposed Facilities: 4, including two of Li and two of Ni o Capital Support Cap: Rs 500 crore per Li beneficiary and Rs 900 crore per Ni beneficiary. About VGF Scheme for Grid-Scale Energy Storage Systems: Target Capacity: The scheme aims to develop 92 Gigawatt-hours (GWh) of additional energy storage capacity, comprising 60 GWh of Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs), 30 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and 2 GWh through alternative storage technologies, with an estimated investment of Rs 97,600 crore. Key Goal: It targets to support the creation of new capacities equivalent to 170% of the present-day grid scale energy storage system capacity in the country and help meet the required Grid Scale ESS capacity of 411 GWh by FY32. Key features: Some of the other key features of the scheme include: • Allocation Method: Under the VGF scheme, energy storage capacity will be allocated to eligible entities through a tariff-based competitive bidding process. • Eligible Entities: Both public and private sector electricity Distribution Companies (DISCOMs) are eligible for VGF support for BESS and Hydro PSP projects, while projects based on alternative energy storage technologies will be implemented by public and private sector entities. • Domestic Content Requirement (DCR): As per the scheme, BESS projects will be subject to a minimum Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) of 40%. This move is expected to promote domestic manufacturing, generate opportunities for Indian industry and complement existing supply-side incentives for battery manufacturing. Approval of Capex Support Scheme: Subsidy Structure: Under the newly approved scheme, the Government of India (GoI) will offer a capital subsidy of 30% of the investment required to set up 4 critical mineral processing units i.e. two Li processing units with minimum capacity of 30,000 tonnes (30kt) each and two Ni processing units with minimum capacity of 50 kt each. Cobalt Recovery: The scheme also envisages recovery of cobalt as a by-product of nickel processing, supporting domestic availability of critical minerals.

Selection Process: The selection of eligible beneficiaries involves a two-stage process i.e. initial assessment of technical qualification; followed by financial bidding where two beneficiaries per mineral are selected based on the least-cost criterion. Disbursement: Under the scheme, the GoI will disburse the incentives in three tranches linked to project milestones. Key Sectors: The scheme is expected to support key sectors such as: electric mobility, BESS, electronics, defence and speciality steel, while strengthening India’s local critical mineral value chain. About Ministry of Mines (MoM): Union Minister- Gangapuram (G.) Kishan Reddy (Constituency- Secunderabad Telangana) Minister of State (MoS)- Satish Chandra Dubey (Rajya Sabha- Bihar) Cabinet Approves Rs. 3,788.04 Crore for Continuation of Fast Track Special Courts Scheme for 5 Years till March 2031 In November 2026, the Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, approved the continuation of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), including exclusive Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Courts, for 5 years from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031, with a total outlay of Rs. 3,788.04 Crore. Exam hints: ✓ What? Cabinet approved the continuation of FTSCs Scheme. ✓ Duration: Five years (FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31). ✓ Total Outlay: Rs. 3,788.04 Crore; Centre – Rs. 2,353.15 Crore & State – Rs. 1,434.89 Crore. ✓ Target: 850 FTSCs, including exclusive POCSO Courts. ✓ Implementing Agency: Department of Justice, MoL&J. ✓ Beneficiaries: Women and child victims of rape and POCSO offences ✓ Other Approval: Two-year additional engagement period for the remaining 75% of Agniveers ✓ Regular Recruitment: 25% of Agniveers will continue to receive regular employment in the Defence Forces based on merit. Background: Launch: The scheme was launched on 2 October 2019 following the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, and the Supreme Court’s directions dated 25 July 2019, which called for exclusive Special Courts in districts with more than 100 pending cases under the POCSO Act, 2012. Administrative Ministry: Implemented by the Department of Justice (DoJ) under the Ministry of Law and Justice (MoL&J). Coverage: The scheme operates across 29 States/Union Territories (UT) with 779 functional FTSCs, including 399 exclusive POCSO Courts, and has disposed of 4,02,457 cases since its launch. Highlights of the Fast Track Special Courts Scheme: Objectives: The scheme aims to ensure time-bound trials, reduce the pendency of rape and POCSO cases, and improve access to justice for women and children Expansion: The number of functional Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs) will increase from 779 to 850, based on case pendency across States and UTs. Financial Allocation: The Government of India will contribute Rs. 2,353.15 Crore, funded through the Nirbhaya Fund, while the State Governments and UTs will contribute Rs. 1,434.89 Crore under the approved CSS funding pattern. Staffing: Each FTSC will have one dedicated Judicial Officer, one Special Public Prosecutor and six support staff to expedite the disposal of pending cases.

Cabinet Approves Two-Year Extension for Agniveers, Enabling Regular Service The Union Cabinet approved an additional two-year engagement period for the remaining 75% of Agniveers after their initial four-year service under the Agnipath Scheme, providing an opportunity for regular enrolment after six years, subject to willingness and prescribed selection criteria, while retaining the existing provision for 25% merit-based regular enrolment after four years. • Enhanced Benefits: The second engagement period will provide higher remuneration, an enhanced Seva Nidhi package and seniority benefits to Agniveers. Performance Assessment: The Armed Forces’ four-year assessment reported positive feedback on Agniveers’ skills, motivation, morale, physical fitness, discipline and technological capabilities. About Ministry of Law and Justice (MoL&J): Minister of State (MoS) (Independent Charge) – Arjun Ram Meghwal (Constituency – Bikaner, Rajasthan) 1st International Maize Conference 2026 Held in Hyderabad to Strengthen Maize Productivity and Sustainability The 1st International Maize Conference was held from 2–4 November 2026 at the JD Convention Centre, Hyderabad, Telangana, bringing together national and international experts to advance maize research, productivity, farmer-centric innovation and sustainable value-chain development. • The conference was organised around the theme “Maize Revolution for Food, Feed, Fodder, Fuel and Sustainability in the Changing World(M4FS)”. Hyderabad, Telangana ✓ Theme? “Maize Revolution for Food, Feed, Fodder, Fuel and Sustainability in the Changing World” ✓ Organisers: MTAI, PJTAU, ICAR, TAAS, CIMMYT, ICAR-IIMR ✓ Production Target: Increase India’s maize production from over 55 million tonnes to 75 million tonnes over the next decade. ✓ 5F Framework: Food, Feed, Fodder, Fuel and Farmers. About 1st International Maize Conference 2026: Organisers: The three-day conference was jointly organised by the Maize Technologists Association of India (MTAI), Professor Jayashankar Telangana Agricultural University (PJTAU), Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Trust for Advancement of Agricultural Sciences (TAAS), International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center (CIMMYT) and ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (ICAR-IIMR). Conference: Bringing together national and international scientists, policymakers, agricultural institutions, universities, and industry stakeholders to advance maize research, enhance productivity, promote farmer- centric innovation, and support sustainable value-chain development. Focus: Key areas included high-yielding varieties and hybrids, improved nutritional quality, resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses, efficient resource utilisation, mechanisation, capacity development, robust seed systems and maize’s contribution to food, feed, fodder and energy security. Production: India’s maize production has reached approximately 55 million tonnes (MT), with substantial productivity gains over the past decade, alongside a target of 75 MT over the next decade through a

Cultivation: Expand maize cultivation across Kharif, Rabi and Spring seasons without affecting oilseeds and pulses, ensuring affordable access to quality seeds, particularly public-sector hybrids. Awards: ICAR and MTAI conferred awards on scientists for outstanding contributions to germplasm conservation, climate-resilient breeding and agronomic innovations, alongside the release of scientific publications during the conference. TRAI Launches ‘Network Anubhav’ Platform to Monitor Network Performance On 4 November 2026, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), Ministry of Communications, launched the ‘Network Anubhav Platform’, a geospatial dashboard integrating user test data with TRAI’s Independent Drive Test (IDT) data and providing a web interface for Do Not Disturb (DND) services. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Network Anubhav Platform launched ✓ Launched by: TRAI ✓ Type: Geospatial and analytical dashboard ✓ Objective: Monitor network performance and improve telecom service quality ✓ Data Sources: MySpeed, MyCall and Independent Drive Tests. About Network Anubhav Platform: Objective: To improve transparency in telecom network performance and enable consumers, Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) and TRAI to assess service quality using location-specific network data. Integration: The platform integrates consumer-generated data from TRAI’s MySpeed and MyCall applications(apps), along with Independent Drive Test (IDT) results, to assess network performance. Key Features: The platform offers an interactive geospatial dashboard to compare network coverage, internet speeds and call quality across locations and operators, with filtering and report-download options. • It also supports the MySpeed Software Development Kit (SDK), enabling third-party applications to integrate internet speed-testing features. About TRAI: Established on 20 February 1997 under the TRAI Act, 1997, TRAI is a statutory regulatory body headquartered in New Delhi, Delhi. Its Chairman is Anil Kumar Lahoti. INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS Bahamas Joins International Solar Alliance as 116th Member Country On 4 November 2026, the Commonwealth of the Bahamas joined the International Solar Alliance (ISA) as its 116th member, following the submission of its Instrument of Accession to the ISA Framework Agreement during the 9th Session of the ISA Assembly in New Delhi, Delhi. Exam Hints: ✓ What? The Bahamas joined the International Solar Alliance (ISA) ✓ Member: 116th member ✓ Which Session? 9th Session of ISA Assembly ✓ Where? New Delhi, India. ✓ Representative: Peter Nicholas Symonette Jr., High Commissioner of the Bahamas. ✓ Received by: P.S. Gangadhar, Joint Secretary, Economic Diplomacy and Head of Depository. Highlights of Bahamas Joining ISA: Formal Accession: The Instrument of Accession was formally handed over by Peter Nicholas Symonette Jr., High Commissioner of the Bahamas, to P.S. Gangadhar, Joint Secretary, Economic Diplomacy and Head of Depository, to strengthen the Bahamas’ participation in international solar energy cooperation. Solar Cooperation: ISA promotes solar energy deployment through knowledge-sharing, technical assistance, collaborative initiatives and investment facilitation, particularly in Least Developed Countries (LDCs) and Small Island Developing States (SIDS). Future Collaboration: Membership enables the Bahamas to participate in ISA programmes, access technical expertise and explore collaborative funding frameworks. About the International Solar Alliance (ISA): Establishment: India and France jointly launched the ISA during the 21st Conference of the Parties (COP21) to the United Nations (UN) Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in Paris in 2015.
